key_insight: Comparing five explanation methods for DeBERTa-v3 shows that explanation agreement is high when the model is confident, but drops sharply in semantically ambiguous medical categories.
clinical_relevance: For medical text classification, the study suggests using multiple explainability methods plus agreement checks to better audit transformer outputs and reduce over-trust in unstable predictions.
method: Zero-shot classification of medical abstracts with DeBERTa-v3 using natural language inference.
Compared SHAP, LIME, occlusion, Input x Gradient, and Attention x Gradient.
Measured explanation agreement with the Jaccard index after standardizing top-token attributions.
evidence_signal: The framework evaluated a balanced sample of 1,000 abstracts per class across five enriched hypotheses per diagnostic category, with accuracy strongest in clear clinical domains and weaker under ambiguity.
watch_item: Top-token attribution and agreement scores may miss nuanced reasoning and can become unstable when categories overlap semantically.
paper_title: A Comparative Explainability Framework for DeBERTa-v3 in Zero-Shot Medical Abstract Classification
